hooks.name: DB Access Guard on Save
hooks.description: When a backend Python file is saved, runs both database-access guards (check_db_imports.py + check_raw_connection.py) against ONLY that single saved file and surfaces any violation in-editor. Advisory only — it does not block the save. Passing the single saved path keeps it instant (no tree scan).

action.prompt:
A backend Python file was just saved. Run BOTH database-access guards against ONLY that single saved file (NOT a full tree scan) so the check is instant, and surface any violation. This is ADVISORY — the save already happened and must not be blocked; just report findings.

Let <saved> be the repo-root-relative POSIX path of the file that was just saved (e.g. `backend/src/services/foo.py`). Run, from the repo root `/home/peter/projects/myAdmin`, both single-file guard invocations against that one path using the backend venv interpreter:

  cd /home/peter/projects/myAdmin && backend/.venv/bin/python backend/scripts/check_db_imports.py <saved>
  cd /home/peter/projects/myAdmin && backend/.venv/bin/python backend/scripts/check_raw_connection.py <saved>

Each script exits 0 (clean) or 1 (violation) and prints `file:line` plus the recommended fix. If EITHER reports a violation, surface it clearly to the user: the offending file:line and the suggested replacement — `import mysql.connector` must go through `from database import DatabaseManager`; a raw `get_connection()` assignment must become `with db.get_cursor() as (cursor, conn):` (reads) or `with db.transaction() as (cursor, conn):` (writes). If both print `[OK]`, say so briefly. Do NOT modify any files, do NOT re-run against the whole tree, and do NOT treat this as blocking — it is fast local feedback only (the authoritative gate is CI).
